- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.  
- Underestimate sharp downward moves when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., > -0.50).  
- Adjust forecasts downward if recent sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment values).  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; lagged sentiment (last 3–5 days) often better predicts direction than immediate sentiment.  
- If forecast peaks exceed true outcome by >5% and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, reduce peak height by 10–15%.  
- Mean-reversion bias is common in 30-day forecasts — if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–8% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid “sentiment-driven overconfidence.”
